To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the helix-8/9 loop of the ERRα ligand-binding domain is a major determinant in the interaction with PGC-1alpha, and that it allosterically links ERRα monomers in a dimer interface to the coactivator binding site.

the helix-8/9 loop of the ERRα ligand binding domain allosterically links homodimer formation with coactivator binding and thereby provides a plausible explanation for the distinct PGC- 1α binding to monomers and homomers of ERRα.

ERRα and ER bind PGC-1 box2 and box3, respectively, and that ERRα binding specificity is determined by its helix 8/9 loop, which allosterically connects the homodimer interface and the coactivator binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel, functionally relevant interactions in nuclear receptor/coactivator complexes and with the structural basis of coactivator selectivity in ERRα.
the structural basis of NR/coactivator interaction and the allosteric communication within the NR LBD.
the identification of a novel allosteric mechanism in NR/ligand/coactivator complexes that may have implications for NR function and drug design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LXXYL motif in PGC-1alpha is a weak coactivator binding motif for ERRalpha.
ERRα and ER bind PGC-1a box3 via different modes, and the helix 4–9 loop plays a major role for this specificity.
the helix loop 8–9 of ERRα is a major determinant for the interaction of the ERRα ligand-binding domain with PGC-1alpha.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the helix8-9 loop is a major determinant for coactivator binding in ERRα, whereas the LXXLL motif is a major determinant in ERα.

in the case of ERRα, the helix 4–5 linker and the helix 6–7 loop are the major determinants of LXXLL binding specificity, whereas the helix 7–8 loop is the major determinant of LXXYL binding specificity.

the ERRα LXXYL-binding site is a composite of two different regions, one being the classical NR box2-binding site and the other the helix 4/helix 8–9 region, and that the helix-4-helix-8–9 loop acts as an interface between the homodimer and coactivator binding surfaces in ERRα.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LBD homomeric interface and the coactivator binding site are functionally connected via the helix 9–10 loop, and that the helix loop 8–9 is a major determinant in NR/ coactivator specificity.

the helix-8–helix-9 loop, which was not previously considered to be important for NR function, is a major specificity element of ERRα and ERβ, and it allosterically links homodimer interface to coactivator binding.
the helix loop 8–9 of ERRα, which is a unique feature of the ERR family of nuclear receptors, is crucial for coactivator specificity and for the regulation of the homodimer interface.
